tasks.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel, which was 1 when this was written and is 2 since round 40, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** was initially left wide on the argument that this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, share an owner, and would gain nothing from narrowing. That argument was later refused -- see the narrowing paragraph below -- and the wildcard is gone. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so the media-engine leaves these tasks genuinely share -- src/index.ts above all -- mean exactly one of this task, PL-0206 and PL-0205's successor PL-0207 can be active at a time. That was originally true of the packages/media-engine/** wildcard and it stayed true after the narrowing, because the overlap is real files rather than a wide prefix. It is a PATH fact and not a capacity one, and the distinction matters now: claude-media's maxParallel was raised from 1 to 2 in round 40, which changes nothing here because these three still share real files, and was done for PL-0601, whose surface is disjoint from all of them. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED FROM packages/media-engine/**, ON THE RULE THE REVIEWER STATED WHEN IT REFUSED PL-0205's WILDCARD: allowedPaths is write ownership, and keeping a wildcard solely because these tasks are already serialised is reservation inflation. The nine media-engine entries are the files this task actually wrote, read out of the implementation: failover.ts and scheduling.ts are the two halves of the policy, the four suites are its regressions, index.ts carries the one export line, vitest.config.ts exists ONLY for this task -- it deselects the wall-clock assertion by name so npm run check stays deterministic -- and package.json carries the ./scheduling export subpath and the bench:failover script, both created here. What is deliberately excluded is the rest of the package, which belongs to PL-0202, PL-0203 and PL-0207. ONE REVIEWDEPENDENCY ADDED, apps/web/src/components/player/playback-machine.ts. It is a CONSUMER rather than this task's work -- it imports scheduleAttempts from @liberty/media-engine/scheduling and schedules without ranking -- but the whole reason scheduling.ts exists as a separate module is that this consumer is a browser bundle edge, and failover.ts's header argues that at length. An approval that did not fingerprint the consumer would stay fresh after someone rewired it, which would silently invalidate the argument for the split. Read-only: this task does not write it, PL-0502 does. REFUSED ON THE MERITS AT 64b631d5, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A TEST WAS PROTECTING THE CLAUSE IT CONTRADICTED. boundedPolicy turned NaN into zero but deliberately left Infinity untouched, on the written argument that an infinite budget is a caller STATING a bound while only NaN is never anything a caller meant. gpt-architect refused that: an infinite budget is not a bound, it is the absence of one wearing a number's clothes. Both policy fields are ordinary numbers, so no cast is needed; attemptsUsed >= Infinity is false forever and count > Infinity is false forever, so under repeated transient failure neither the global nor the per-candidate condition ever terminates -- the unbounded reload loop pointed at a CDN that this module's own header says it exists to prevent, reached through the front door instead of through arithmetic. It directly contradicts the single acceptance clause, that retry and fallback behaviour is BOUNDED. THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING IS THE TEST. failover.test.ts pinned maxAttempts: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY as intended behaviour, with a comment restating the wrong argument. A regression suite agreeing with the code is not evidence that either is right, and this one was written to protect the clause it broke. THE FIX GENERALISES THE RULE RATHER THAN ADDING A CASE: boundedPolicy now delegates to an enforceableBudget helper that asks Number.isFinite, so the question is whether a number can bound anything at all rather than which exceptional values somebody thought of. Written as an allowlist for the same reason every other gate here is one -- NaN and the two infinities are the whole set today, but enumerating them would be a denylist over the numbers, and a denylist fails open on whatever it missed. A negative or zero budget is still passed through untouched, because that really is a caller stating a bound of nothing. Four regressions replace the one that was wrong: an infinite attempt budget, an infinite per-candidate retry budget, a NEGATIVE infinity that no enumeration of named values would have caught, and a finite budget passed through unchanged so the other three cannot pass by the guard simply zeroing everything. All three machine gates are re-recorded because the scheduler itself changed, including the bench performance gate, which the reviewer noted really had executed the timed test rather than inheriting the ordinary suite's exclusion. PROVENANCE WAS ACCEPTED, and separately the reviewer ruled on the shared introduction commit: this task and PL-0207 genuinely began in the same historical commit 4091a2b, a commit is not required to be task-atomic when recovering old history, and what matters is that the lower bound is truthful and the current review surface honest. No successor, no later base, no artificial path trimming -- record that the introduction commit is shared and leave it alone. THIS PARAGRAPH AND THE FOUR BEFORE IT SPENT TWO ROUNDS ON PL-0207'S RECORD BY MISTAKE, because the Edit anchors matched a nearly identical sentence there and neither edit was checked against the record it landed on. They are here now, and the mistake is recorded on PL-0207 rather than quietly erased. The lesson is small and general: an anchor that is unique in a diff is not necessarily unique in a file.

The health mechanism was already implemented and correct in 67c5fc9 and 6c31298; what was missing was DETECTION, and a 31-mutant campaign found five places the suite would have stayed green against a wrong implementation. THE SHARPEST IS CLAUSE 5, AND IT IS A REAL HOLE THAT WAS CLOSED: the suite was strong on the mapper and BLIND ON BOTH ADAPTERS. 'public-domain' : source.rights -- survived all 275 tests in stremio/client.ts (M21), again for rightsBasis (M24), and again in fixture/provider.ts where the verdict is permanently unknown so the rewrite fires on EVERY candidate it produces (M25). tasks.title: Auth integration decision
tasks.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS BOTH NARROWED AND WIDENED, AND THE WIDENING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. As declared, this task reserved docs/**, apps/web/src/** and packages/contracts/** -- all twenty-one documents, the entire web application and the whole contracts package -- for a decision record. Each of those three prefix-contains an active task's write surface, so a P0 that is already finished in the tree could not be claimed by anyone. Worse, and in the opposite direction, packages/auth/** was NOT declared at all, yet nine files there are this task's primary output: a reconcile-existing run would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. Both errors come from declaring a surface by guess before the work exists rather than from reading it afterwards. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and only the control-plane record lags, the same pattern as PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0601. All four acceptance clauses are met: packages/auth exports the seam at . and ./server with better-auth a dependency of that package alone; sessions are database-backed through @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts carries ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES with findSurfaceViolations defaulting unknown plugins to violations; and both better-auth and its adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret, asserted by enabled-surface.test.ts against REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. The decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md, which self-labels Proposed because claude-lead wrote it and WAS also this task's reviewAgent when it was written -- that is no longer true, see the reviewAgent change below, and the label should be revisited by whoever closes this task. TWO HONEST CAVEATS STATED IN THE ADR RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and neither is an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed against a database, because there is no PostgreSQL anywhere in this environment; and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. PROVENANCE: this must be started with --reconcile-existing, not against HEAD. The probe is packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts -- but after the PL-0205 finding, a filename probe is not enough on its own: whoever reconciles it must confirm the candidate base tree contains neither ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES nor WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES anywhere, so a file created by a later move cannot open the range after the behaviour it claims to cover. REVIEWAGENT MOVED FROM claude-lead TO gpt-architect. This task carries a security-review gate on an authentication boundary, and its decision record was written by claude-lead. A reviewer that is also the author is not a reviewer; routing it outward makes the review stricter rather than looser, which is the only direction this may be changed in. THE MIGRATION IS A REVIEWDEPENDENCY, AND THE REVIEWER MADE THAT A CONDITION OF CLAIMING. It observed that this record cites packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql as the factual basis for the database-backed-session clause while the file sat in no part of the declared surface, and gave two defensible resolutions and one forbidden one: add it as a reviewDependency, or stop using it as evidence and let the Drizzle adapter and configuration carry the clause alone -- but do not mix the two. Its words: either is defensible; mixing the two is not. Resolved as a reviewDependency, because the ADR genuinely does rest on it: ADR-007 argues database-backed sessions over stateless ones partly on the shape of that migration, and an approval that did not fingerprint it could stay fresh after the schema underneath the argument changed. It is deliberately NOT an allowedPath -- this task did not write it, PL-0402 did, and reviewDependencies exist precisely so a boundary a task depends on can be reviewed without being reserved. No collision follows: reviewDependencies reserve nothing, so PL-0402 may still declare packages/persistence/** as a write surface whenever it is claimed.

tasks.title: Profile model
tasks.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

tasks.title: Progress persistence
tasks.acceptance: Progress rows are scoped to a profile id rather than a user id and keyed by (profileId, contentId) so a repeated write upserts idempotently, with read and write authorized against the active profile; two devices writing the same title are resolved by a server-issued writer epoch rather than by client timestamps or by a monotonically-increasing-position rule, because client clocks are unreliable and a monotonic rule wrongly refuses a legitimate rewind; and writes go directly to PostgreSQL, with no Redis write-behind introduced until a PostgreSQL problem has actually been measured

tasks.title: Watchlist persistence
tasks.acceptance: Typed add, remove, and list APIs with authorization

tasks.title: Playback session API
tasks.acceptance: Server resolves authorized provider candidates and clients cannot submit arbitrary media URLs; the session response is a discriminated union on outcome (granted, denied, unavailable) with reasons present on every branch rather than as an optional field, because a denial with no reason trail violates the reason-trail invariant exactly as much as a grant with none

tasks.title: Player state machine
tasks.acceptance: The machine models the session and candidate lifecycle (resolving, loading a candidate, playing, buffering, seeking, recovering, failing over, ended, fatal) rather than UI state, which the controls layer already owns; the video element and the playback engine stay authoritative and the machine is a validated projection of them, so every engine and media event has an inbound transition even in states where it supposedly cannot occur. MANDATORY CONSOLIDATION, added 2026-09-18 by gpt-architect's round-48 direction when it approved PL-0903 and PL-0904. The reviewer was explicit that these are NOT reasons to reopen either of those tasks: PL-0502 owns the whole player surface and finishes the consolidation while implementing the machine. (1) RENAME browser_unsupported to an engine-neutral lifecycle reason, host_unsupported, as a COMPLETE migration -- type member, controller, machine, tests, reason trail, docs and comments -- with NO alias kept. One lifecycle fact gets one name. Behaviour is unchanged: the engine loaded and ran far enough to determine that the current host cannot support it. (2) TIGHTEN EngineState's unavailable variant from `detail?: EngineUnavailableDetail` to `detail: EngineUnavailableDetail | null`. Every producer must state whether detail was established; omission must not be the unknown representation. This is the same required-and-nullable discipline the contracts already apply to licenseUrl and to media facts. (3) UNIFY the duplicate engine-id vocabularies. PlaybackEngineId and PlaybackErrorEngine describe the same two values. Make one authoritative and derive or alias the other in the dependency-safe direction the code comments already identify. Two independently editable literal unions for one engine identity must not remain. (4) DO NOT WEAKEN PL-0904 while integrating: never make native code/category `number | null`; do not flatten mpvError into Shaka-numbered fields; do not invent a native failure classification without evidence; keep aborted engine control flow out of candidate failure accounting. tasks.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.

THE EXACT DEFECT THIS MUST CATCH, preserved as the regression case: apps/web/src/lib/server-bootstrap.ts imported @liberty/media-inspection/node/pinned-fetch while apps/web/package.json declared seven @liberty packages and not that one. It reached a reviewer because NO EXISTING GATE CAN SEE IT: the import resolves through the root workspace symlink, so typecheck, lint, build and the unit suites were green, and even npm ci --dry-run returned 0 because npm tolerates a link node that already exists. It was found by a human reader, which is not a detection mechanism. Required of the check: it reads each workspace's own manifest rather than the root's; it resolves subpath imports (@liberty/x/node/y declares @liberty/x); it covers test files as well as source, since server-bootstrap.test.ts carried the same undeclared import; and it fails the build rather than warning, because a warning in a green pipeline is how this one survived. A dry-run install against a populated node_modules does NOT satisfy this and must not be offered as the implementation. NOT IN SCOPE: the reverse direction (a declared dependency nothing imports) is a different and much weaker signal, and adding it would make the check noisy enough to be turned off. SECOND SCOPE ADDITION 2026-09-22, on gpt-architect's ruling at cd6f3efd46a75a150206617a2fa6bf747a1c3a5b: 'CI must not rely on typecheck and build racing successfully when typecheck consumes files build writes.' THE DEFECT, verified structurally rather than inferred from a flake: apps/web/tsconfig.json line 15 includes .next/types/**/*.ts; turbo.json's build task declares .next/** as an output; and turbo.json's typecheck task declares dependsOn ['^typecheck'] with NO edge to build. So tsc and next build race on that directory whenever both run in one graph. HOW IT SURFACED, because the shape of the evidence matters: a single @liberty/web#typecheck exit 2 with NO 'error TS' line in the output, which passed on two re-runs of the identical tree. The command that produced it -- npx turbo run typecheck lint build --force -- had been this project's recorded gate invocation for several rounds and had passed every time, which is what a race looks like until it does not. The lead changed its own procedure to three separate invocations, which removes the race from the evidence but NOT from CI. Required: CI must not be able to run the two concurrently in a way that lets a typecheck read a partially written .next/types. The mechanism is the implementer's -- a dependsOn edge from typecheck to build, a separate tsconfig for the check that excludes generated types, or sequencing in the workflow -- but a green run is not evidence the race is gone, so whatever is chosen must be demonstrated by argument from the task graph rather than by re-running until it passes. NOT IN SCOPE: fixing the unrelated pre-existing env:validate warnings. SMALLER AND RELATED, folded in here rather than filed: turbo.json's globalEnv lists none of the LIBERTY_CATALOG_* variables, including the eight predating round 63. Harmless today because they are read at runtime by instrumentation.ts rather than at build time, so it affects only build-cache hashing -- but a variable that is read at build time later and still unlisted would let one cache entry serve builds that meant different values, which is the defect env:validate already warns about for LIBERTY_FIXTURE_MEDIA_ORIGIN.

tasks.title: A real catalog metadata source
tasks.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
tasks.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.

tasks.title: Fixture provider states the protection fact it actually knows
tasks.acceptance: The fixture provider adapter emits contentProtection { state: "clear" } for its own candidates, because for a fixture the absence of DRM is a fact the adapter genuinely knows rather than something it is guessing. Created from gpt-architect's round-44 non-blocking finding on PL-0501, in the reviewer's own words: "Create a provider-owned task for the fixture provider protection fact. The fixture adapter, not PL-0501, should emit { state: \"clear\" } when that fact is genuinely known. PL-0501 may keep PROTECTION_NOT_STATED as the conservative fallback until that provider task lands." So the deliverable is a narrowing of where the fact is asserted, not a behaviour change in routing: PROTECTION_NOT_STATED stays in PL-0501 as the fallback for every adapter that has not stated a protection fact, and this task removes the fixture from the set that needs it. Required, and each is a way this task could be done wrongly: the fixture must set the field itself rather than PL-0501 special-casing the fixture provider id, because a consumer branching on a provider identity is exactly the provider-specific logic outside @liberty/provider-sdk that invariant 3 forbids; requiresContentDecryptionModule must be observed returning false for a fixture candidate and the observation recorded, since state !== "clear" is the whole point of the encoding and an untested clear is indistinguishable from an untested unknown; the fallback path in PL-0501 must be left in place and a test must still cover an adapter that states nothing, because deleting the fallback once its only current user stops needing it would fail open for the next adapter; and no other adapter may be given a protection fact here, because for a real provider the honest value is unknown and asserting clear for one would be a rights misstatement rather than a defaulting decision. Out of scope: any change to contract shape (PL-0902 owns it), to ranking (@liberty/media-engine), or to capability routing.

tasks.title: Catalog ingestion is scheduled and stored, not re-run per query
tasks.acceptance: Catalog answers are served from stored ingested state refreshed on a schedule, rather than by running a full ingestion pass per query. TODAY THE ADAPTER RUNS ONE FULL runIngestionPass PER QUERY, which is correct for a seam and wrong for a deployment: it makes every page view an outbound crawl, ties response time to an upstream service, and scales the load on that service with this product's traffic. Required: the freshness and next-pass planning PL-0305 already built is what DRIVES the schedule rather than being recomputed alongside it; an answer still carries its age and stated staleness policy, so nothing becomes fresher by being cached; tombstones survive a refresh, because a work withdrawn upstream must not reappear from stored state; a refresh that fails leaves the previous state served AND SAYS SO, rather than emptying the catalog or silently serving stale data as current; and rights and availability are re-evaluated against stored records rather than trusted from the pass that stored them, since a rights basis can lapse. The reviewer noted that PL-0305 is NOT to be described as having delivered a deployed ingestion worker; this task is where that claim would become true.

tasks.title: A configured catalog with nothing usable does not look empty
tasks.acceptance: The user-facing catalog path preserves the distinction the port now makes between no_records_usable and catalog_empty. apps/web/src/lib/catalog.ts maps an empty array to 'empty' and therefore COLLAPSES THE TWO, which is the one place PL-0305's four-state work stops short of the user. The two states have different causes and different remedies: catalog_empty means the source has nothing, while no_records_usable means records exist and every one of them was withheld -- almost always for want of an operator rights basis, which is an operator action rather than a user problem. tasks.title: A resumed pass may not infer absence: fix what `complete` means
tasks.acceptance: `complete` means THE WHOLE SOURCE WAS OBSERVED, sufficient to infer absence -- not merely that this invocation reached end-of-enumeration. THE HAZARD, stated exactly. `IngestionPassResult.complete` is set when the provider's cursor runs out. A pass started from a non-null `resumeCursor` can reach that end having DELIBERATELY SKIPPED every page before the cursor, and it reports `complete: true`. `reconcileTombstones` takes `complete` as licence to infer absence, so every known content id living on a skipped page is unseen, is inferred withdrawn, and is mass-tombstoned. Under PL-0309's tombstone rule a tombstone is released only by a later complete pass that accepts the work again, so the damage is not self-healing on the next pass. WHY THIS IS NOT LIVE TODAY, and why that is not a reason to defer it: PL-0309's `schedule.ts` always passes `resumeCursor: null`, which keeps the hazard unreachable at the cost of re-reading the prefix every pass. The reviewer ruled it non-blocking for PL-0309 on exactly that ground and required this task BEFORE resume support is enabled. So the ordering constraint is the deliverable as much as the fix is: whoever adds resume must find this already closed. REQUIRED: absence inference is gated on a fact that a resumed pass cannot satisfy by accident. The implementer chooses the mechanism and states why -- a distinct field separating 'enumeration ended' from 'whole source observed', a fourth `TombstoneWithholdReason` for a resumed pass, or a `seenContentIds` set that makes the reconciliation exact rather than inferential. What is NOT acceptable is a comment telling a future caller not to resume, which is the state this task exists to replace. REQUIRED: a regression that fails against today's code. Start a pass from a `resumeCursor` positioned past a known id, let it run to the provider's end, and assert that id is NOT tombstoned. That test goes red on the current tree -- verify it does and say so -- which makes this a genuine red-to-green rather than a restatement. CONSIDER AND RULE ON, rather than silently skipping: `IngestionPassResult` publishes no seen set, and refusals carry native ids rather than derived content ids, so PL-0309 could not distinguish 'the complete pass saw this work and refused it' from 'never saw it' and took the conservative reading. If `seenContentIds` is the mechanism chosen here, say what it does to that narrowing. NOT IN SCOPE: enabling resume, backfill, or paging beyond `maxPages`; changing the tombstone-RELEASE rule PL-0309 delivered and the reviewer accepted; and redesigning `CatalogStore`, `applyPassToSnapshot` or `refreshCatalogIfDue`.

The reviewer agreed and ordered it separately. rights-review is on the gate list because a wrongly tombstoned work is a catalog that silently loses licensed content, and the release rule means it stays lost until a complete pass re-accepts it.

ORDERING IS REPORTING PRECEDENCE AND IS TESTED: a resumed pass that also ran out of page budget reports resumed_pass rather than page_limit_reached, because the prefix was skipped by choice and raising maxPages would not fix it. Publishing the set would matter only to the STORE, which today releases a tombstone when a complete pass ACCEPTS a work and could then release when a complete pass merely SAW it -- a change to the tombstone-release rule the reviewer accepted in PL-0309 and explicitly out of this task's scope. Shipping an unread field to enable a rule change nobody has approved is the wrong order; the argument a later task should answer is written into docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md rather than left in a commit message. WHAT THIS DOES NOT TURN ON: resume and backfill remain off, schedule.ts still passes resumeCursor null, and LIBERTY_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES still bounds the catalog a reader sees. What changed is that enabling resume is now a scheduling decision rather than a mass-deletion risk.

tasks.acceptance: The production playback-session route refuses a request body above a declared bound before parsing it, and the refusal carries a reason code that exists in the contract. TODAY IT READS AN UNBOUNDED BODY: apps/web/src/app/api/v1/playback/session/playback-session-implementation.ts reads the body with no cap while the development-only resolve scaffold beside it caps one, so the production path is the weaker of the two. Required: the bound is a named constant with the reason for its value, not a magic number; the reason code is added to the contract and to docs/API_CONTRACTS.md in the same change; the refusal happens BEFORE the body is buffered, because a cap enforced after reading the whole body does not bound memory; a regression drives a body over the bound through the real route and observes the refusal, and a second drives one just under it and observes normal handling, since a cap that refuses everything is indistinguishable from an outage. Out of scope: the candidate-id bound, which is PL-0708, and any change to what a well-formed request means.

tasks.title: Stream candidate fields carry length bounds

MEASURED, not hypothesised: a 1,000,000-character candidate id produced a 2,002,555-byte response during the PL-0702 review. The bound belongs in the contract rather than at the route, because every consumer of a candidate inherits it there and a per-route cap is one route away from being forgotten. Required: each bounded field's limit is justified against a real identifier rather than picked round -- state what the longest legitimate value looks like; a property test asserts no candidate accepted by the schema can exceed the response budget; and the change is checked against the fixture and Wikidata sources, because a bound that rejects a legitimate upstream id is an outage, not a fix. THE RISK THIS TASK CARRIES: streamCandidateSchema is the ranker's input and PL-0902 extends it; a bound set too low silently drops candidates and the reason trail must say so rather than showing an empty list. Out of scope: the request body bound (PL-0707).

REQUIRED, extraction half: the canonical host and IP classification vocabulary and its normalisation move into @liberty/net-policy; provider-sdk consumes that shared classifier; media-inspection consumes that shared classifier; PL-0709's deep cross-package test import is REMOVED; and the agreement test becomes unnecessary as two implementations become one -- replace it with tests of the shared classifier PLUS package-boundary tests proving both consumers actually import it, because an extraction nothing imports is a third copy rather than a merge. ALSO IN SCOPE BECAUSE THE EXTRACTION PUTS IT IN PLAY: pin.ts's normaliseHost does not fold the DNS root label. tasks.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
tasks.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. IMPLEMENTED IN ROUND 45, AND IT IS THE ONLY TASK IN THE RECOVERY CAMPAIGN THAT NEEDED NO PROVENANCE WORK AT ALL -- genuinely unstarted, so an ordinary start captures a true base. THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL, WITH NO REGISTRY VENDORED, exactly as the script rule already is. A new spokenLanguage helper answers which language will come out of the speakers rather than which subtag a string starts with, and it differs from primarySubtag in precisely one place: where a macrolanguage has been narrowed by an extended-language subtag. BCP-47 spells a language as 2*3ALPHA optionally followed by an extlang of exactly 3ALPHA, while a region is two letters or three DIGITS and a script is four letters, so three ASCII letters immediately after a two- or three-letter primary is unambiguously an extlang and nothing else can take that shape in that position. RFC 5646 permanently invalidates the second and third extlang positions, so there is at most one to find. THE COLLAPSE RUNS TOWARD THE SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THE GENERAL, which is what makes the equivalence clause work in both directions: zh-cmn becomes cmn rather than zh, so the prefixed and bare spellings of one language agree, and the equivalence survives any region or script suffix because those subtags are never consulted. A bare zh stays zh -- it names the macrolanguage and neither variety, so treating it as either would invent a preference the viewer did not express, which is the same asymmetry the script rule uses when it says a tag naming no script conflicts with nothing. THE NEW OUTCOME IS ITS OWN REASON, as the acceptance requires: preferred_language_other_variety_only, distinct from preferred_language_other_script_only and from the regional fallback, because the three have different remedies -- a script conflict is about READING and the dialogue is still the viewer's, a regional difference is cosmetic and is still selected, and this one is the wrong language. Reporting it as a regional fallback would move the defect out of the matcher and into the vocabulary. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING THAT THE DESIGN MADE TRUE BY ACCIDENT AND THE TESTS NOW PIN: the script and variety findings are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than merely ordered. matchesOnlyAcrossScripts requires a match under ignore_script, setting the script aside leaves the spoken-language comparison, and a different variety fails it -- so zh-yue-Hant against a zh-cmn-Hans preference is not across both boundaries, it is simply the wrong language and the script question is moot. Only a track in the viewer's own spoken language can be across the script boundary, which is the only case where a font is the remedy. EXERCISED THROUGH BOTH CONSUMERS, which the acceptance demands because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift, and the way that guarantee fails is one being corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under the new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. TWO PROPERTIES HAD TO BE TIGHTENED RATHER THAN MERELY KEPT PASSING, and that is the most useful thing this task turned up. Both audio.property.test.ts and subtitles.property.test.ts asserted that a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which was a restatement of the rule being removed; once zh-cmn and cmn are both in languageTagArb it is simply false, since that is one spoken language with two primary subtags. Both now ask spokenLanguage, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher actually makes. The arbitrary gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
tasks.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

Equivalence is pinned in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one, and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix -- and a bare zh is refused against either variety, because it names the macrolanguage and neither. Shape confusion is pinned negatively: a region, a script, a variant and a private-use singleton are none of them read as an extlang. ONE EXISTING ASSERTION WAS REVERSED RATHER THAN ADDED TO, and it is recorded as such in the test: zh-cmn-hans-cn against zh-hant under ignore_script used to expect a match and now expects none, because that is exactly the conflation this task removes. TWO PROPERTIES WERE TIGHTENED. Both suites asserted a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which restated the rule being removed and is false once cmn and zh-cmn are both generated; both now assert spokenLanguage equality, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher makes. languageTagArb gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it.

ReviewDependencies may legitimately preexist and a write surface may contain unrelated older material, but any earlier delta that is itself part of the task means the candidate base is too late. The practical form: for each declared write path, list the commits touching it that are ancestors of the candidate base, and refuse the base if any is attributable to this task -- the cheapest mechanical signal being the task id in the commit message, with the remainder left for inspection rather than decided by the runner. THE SWEEP REFUSED ITSELF TWICE, AND THE TWO REFUSALS MEANT DIFFERENT THINGS. The first was a bug: it read git log --oneline, which prints only the subject, while this repository writes task ids into commit BODIES, so it would have found no task id on any path and cleared every base for the wrong reason. The second, after that was fixed, was not a bug at all -- it was the check refusing a FALSE PREMISE I had built into its own positive control. I had asserted that PL-0601 must be findable in the history of docs/LIVE_TV.md, on the strength of the reviewer's sentence that bbe68ed8 replaced the original eleven-line Live TV note with the PL-0601 normalization-and-rights document. tasks.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. THE SURFACE THIS IMPLIES IS WIDER THAN THIS TASK CURRENTLY DECLARES, AND THAT IS SETTLED BEFORE THE CLAIM RATHER THAN DISCOVERED DURING IT. The reviewer offered two levels: at minimum make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability, use issuance identity as well. The minimum is NOT ACHIEVABLE IN THE TYPE SYSTEM, and PL-0706 already established why: a spread copies a branded property along with everything else and type-checks with no cast at all, so only object identity rejects it. TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable. Therefore the runtime registry is not the optional upper level here, it is the only level that works -- and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ASK. The consumers are in another package: packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts and watchlist-repository.ts read scope.profileId straight into their predicates, and profile-repository.ts and repository-scoping.test.ts also handle the type. So this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration, and it will then overlap PL-0402, PL-0403 and PL-0404, which are BACKLOG today and must be sequenced after it. The alternative -- brand and registry in packages/auth with no consumer asking -- would produce a capability that looks unforgeable and is not, which is worse than the present state because it would read as fixed. Whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. tasks.title: Supersession is a field, and a task cannot stay gated behind one
tasks.description: Four tasks -- PL-0205, PL-0401, PL-0601, PL-0703 -- are BLOCKED, terminal, and superseded by a corrective re-run. Each says so only in prose. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED, so a superseded task can never reach DONE, and with completion.requireAllDependenciesDone true, any task depending on one is gated forever. That is not a hypothetical: PL-0301 was gated behind PL-0205 while PL-0207 sat DONE, and with it PL-0302, PL-0501, PL-0502, PL-0701 and PL-0702. A human noticed. Nothing in ai:validate could have.
tasks.notes: SCOPE IS THE VALIDATOR, NOT A DEPENDENCY REWRITER. The rule reports; it never edits a dependency, because repointing a dependency is a task-definition change and those are deliberate, reasoned and recorded -- see PL-0301's own notes for what that looks like. An automatic repointer would make the graph self-modifying on the strength of a field any writer can set. THE RULE, PRECISELY. For each task T declaring supersededBy S: S must exist, must not be T, and T must not itself be DONE, or that is an ERROR, because a DONE task that claims to be superseded is two contradictory records of the same work. If S declares supersedes, it must name T -- a one-way pointer is a typo waiting to be trusted. Then, for each task D whose dependencies contain T: if S is DONE, ERROR, because D is gated behind a task that can never complete while its replacement already has; if S is not DONE, WARN, because the edge is not yet fatal but will become so the moment S completes, and a warning that arrives before the deadlock is the entire point. WHY ERROR AND NOT WARN FOR THE FIRST CASE. ai:validate already treats provenance drift as a warning and structural impossibility as an error. A dependency that can never be satisfied is structural: no sequence of legal transitions resolves it. It belongs with 'missing dependency' and 'invalid status', not with drift. WHAT THIS RULE CANNOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY OVERTRUSTS IT. supersededBy is self-asserted, exactly like fromAgent on the agent bus. It proves that somebody wrote a pointer, not that the successor genuinely carries the predecessor's work. A wrong pointer produces a wrong error or hides a real deadlock. It is a cheap alarm on a failure mode that has already cost this project one stalled milestone, not a proof of anything.
tasks.acceptance: ai:validate refuses a task graph in which a task depends on a task that declares supersededBy and whose named successor is DONE, and warns when the successor is not yet DONE. It also refuses a supersededBy naming a missing task, naming itself, declared on a DONE task, or contradicted by the successor's supersedes field. The rule reports and never edits a dependency. The four existing supersession pairs validate clean, and a regression in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs proves the rule fires -- both that it errors on a reconstructed PL-0301-behind-PL-0205 graph and that it stays silent on the repaired one, so it cannot pass by being inert.

tasks.title: Windows desktop shell and the PlayerAdapter boundary
tasks.description: Project Liberty's first production target is Windows desktop on the commander's own machine. The commander has settled the direction: a Tauri shell, the existing Next.js application preserved rather than rewritten and served by a Next standalone sidecar, a PlayerAdapter boundary the application and domain layers depend on instead of any concrete player, libmpv for compatible non-DRM playback, Shaka/EME retained for DRM-capable playback, capability routing made explicit before playback rather than discovered during it, and an LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline of our own rather than a GPL prebuilt. This task records that decision and specifies the boundary. It writes documentation only -- no shell, no adapter, no dependency is added here, because the instruction is that architecture is recorded before a large irreversible implementation, not after it.
tasks.notes: THE AUDIT CAME FIRST AND IT FOUND A CLEAN SLATE. A repository-wide search for electron, tauri, mpv, libmpv, webview2, neutralino and nw.js across every .ts, .tsx, .json, .md, .mjs and .yml outside node_modules returned nothing. So neither shell was favoured by anything already in the tree, and the decision was made on evidence rather than on inertia. Today's player is shaka-player ~5.2.6 with xstate ^5.32.5 and custom-media-element in apps/web. THE DECIDING FACT IS COMPOSITING, NOT BUNDLE SIZE. Putting HTML chrome over a hardware-accelerated native video surface in one window on Windows is a documented, shipping arrangement on WebView2 -- ICoreWebView2Controller2::put_DefaultBackgroundColor accepts alpha 0 or 255 only, and at 0 the host's content renders beneath -- and has no supported path on Chromium, where PPAPI is gone and child HWNDs are no longer in the window hierarchy. Stremio ships the WebView2 plus libmpv --wid arrangement in production on Windows and measured its previous render-API-into-a-texture approach as 2-5x worse. Any size-based argument for Tauri should be dropped: with a Node sidecar the installer lands near Electron's anyway. THE SIDECAR IS WHAT PRESERVES THE APPLICATION. Tauri's default is a static export, which would force every /api/v1 route handler off Next -- a rewrite of the application's architecture, which the instruction forbids. output: standalone in a sidecar keeps Server Components, route handlers, proxy.ts, cookies(), headers(), Server Actions and ISR working. It costs a Node runtime in the bundle, a loopback listener, supervision code and Tauri's CSP injection, which does not reach an external http origin. ONE QUESTION THIS TASK DOES NOT DECIDE AND MUST NOT DECIDE SILENTLY. A sidecar runs the application's server on a machine the user administers. If provider resolution runs there, then the boundary that enforces invariants 1 and 2 executes from files the user can read and replace, with whatever credentials it needs in its environment. The alternative is that the desktop build implements those specific routes as an authenticated proxy to the backend -- same route, same contract, same URL, a different implementation behind it, selected by build target, which is ordinary adapter work rather than a rewrite. This document states the question, states the recommendation, and leaves the ruling to the reviewer and the commander. It is a design input to PL-0501 and is cheaper to supply now than to retrofit. DRM IS A ROUTING CONSTRAINT, NOT A GAP TO CLOSE. mpv has no CDM and cannot be given one. That is not something to work around: the mpv adapter must REFUSE a DRM-protected candidate with a named reason and must never attempt it, never fall back and never degrade. Which means capability routing has to be an explicit, reasoned decision before playback -- canPlay returning a reason on both branches -- rather than a guess discovered at load time. That is what makes invariant 2 structural here rather than a promise, and it is why the boundary carries a capability descriptor at all. THE LICENSING WORK IS THE LONG POLE AND IT GATES SHIPPING RATHER THAN PROTOTYPING. A stock prebuilt libmpv is a GPL build and must not ship in a closed-source product; the one LGPL variant on offer statically links an LGPLv3 FFmpeg and carries its builder's own no-warranty disclaimer. Building our own with -Dgpl=false and an LGPL FFmpeg, with an SBOM, converts an open-ended exposure into a reviewable artifact. Nothing in this document is legal advice and counsel review is named as a precondition of shipping rather than assumed.
tasks.acceptance: A recorded architecture decision states the Windows desktop target, the Tauri shell, the preserved Next.js application served by a standalone sidecar, and the LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline, each with the evidence it rests on and the strongest argument against it. tasks.title: DRM capability on the candidate and playback-session contract
tasks.description: packages/contracts/src contains no occurrence of drm, widevine, playready or eme -- verified by grep across the whole source tree on 2026-09-15. So a resolved candidate carries no statement about whether it is encrypted, under which system, or against which license server. PL-0901 makes that a blocking gap rather than a cosmetic one: the desktop build routes between an mpv adapter that has no CDM and cannot be given one, and a Shaka/EME adapter that has one, and PlayerAdapter.canPlay is required to return a REASON on both branches rather than a boolean guess. A reasoned decision cannot be made from a contract that carries no field to reason about, so this gates the capability routing in PL-0901 section 4.
tasks.notes: THE SHAPE IS A CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR, NOT A BOOLEAN. An isDrm flag would answer the routing question and nothing else; the adapter also has to say WHY it refused, and a reason trail that says drm_required with no system named is not debuggable, which is invariant 4. The reviewer should expect at minimum the protection system and, where the boundary knows it, the license acquisition endpoint -- and should rule on whether an UNKNOWN encryption state is representable, because absent is not the same as none. A candidate whose encryption state was never established must not read as clear; that is the same required-and-nullable discipline PL-0207 established for media facts, and the precedent is deliberate. WHERE IT LIVES IS PART OF THE QUESTION. The descriptor could sit on streamCandidate, on the playback-session response, or on both with one deriving from the other. The candidate is what the ranker scores and the session is what the player is handed, and PL-0301's implementation already argues at packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/provider.ts that the playable address belongs on the session rather than the candidate, for a reason that may or may not extend to the key system. Settle it before writing it. NOTHING HERE MAY WEAKEN A PROTECTION. This task describes encryption so the correct player is chosen and so a refusal is explainable. It adds no decryption, no key handling and no fallback that would attempt a protected source with an engine that has no CDM -- invariant 2 -- and the mpv adapter's refusal must stay a refusal rather than becoming a degraded attempt. SEQUENCING: overlaps PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 on packages/contracts and must be sequenced after whichever is active. It should land before PL-0501 writes the session response, because retrofitting a discriminated field into a shipped contract is the change PL-0501's own acceptance warns about.
tasks.acceptance: A resolved stream candidate, or the playback session that carries it, states its content-protection requirement explicitly: the protection system where one applies, an unencrypted state that is asserted rather than inferred from an absent field, and an UNKNOWN state that is representable and does not read as unencrypted. PlayerAdapter.canPlay can decide routing from the contract alone, without inspecting a URL, a manifest or a provider-specific field, and can name the protection system in its refusal reason. Adding the field changes no existing candidate's meaning by accident: a candidate that omits it is refused by the schema rather than defaulted to clear. Provider-specific spellings stay inside @liberty/provider-sdk and are normalized before they reach the contract. No decryption, key handling or protection bypass is added.

tasks.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
tasks.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
tasks.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
tasks.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

tasks.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
tasks.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
tasks.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
tasks.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.
